title: Hypertensive emergency needing arteriolar dilation + improved renal perfusion/natriuresis: fenoldopam (dopamine-1 agonist)
vignette: A 43-year-old man comes to the emergency department due to a 3-day history of persistent headaches. The patient has a history of hypertension and has had poor medical follow-up. Blood pressure is 224/115 mm Hg and pulse is 67/min. He appears mildly confused during the physical examination, but no focal neurologic deficits are noted. Funduscopic examination shows bilateral papilledema. Serum creatinine is 1.4 mg/dL. An intravenous medication is initiated that causes arteriolar dilation while also improving renal perfusion and increasing natriuresis. Which of the following agents is most likely being used in this patient?

clues.note: Severe hypertension (>=180/120) with end-organ damage (confusion, papilledema, elevated creatinine) is a HYPERTENSIVE EMERGENCY requiring controlled IV blood pressure reduction.
Papilledema (plus encephalopathy and renal injury) confirms acute end-organ damage - the hallmark of hypertensive emergency.

clues.text: arteriolar dilation while also improving renal perfusion and increasing natriuresis
clues.note: An IV agent that dilates arterioles AND boosts renal perfusion/natriuresis is FENOLDOPAM (a selective dopamine-1 receptor agonist).

whatMatters: A hypertensive emergency treated with an IV agent that causes arteriolar dilation PLUS improved RENAL PERFUSION and NATRIURESIS = FENOLDOPAM, a selective peripheral DOPAMINE-1 receptor agonist - useful when renal function is a concern. Answer B.
strategy: Match the unique pharmacology: arteriolar vasodilation + increased renal perfusion + natriuresis = fenoldopam (D1 agonist -> cAMP -> vasodilation of arterial beds including renal). Reject agents lacking these renal benefits: esmolol (beta-1 blocker, no vasodilation/renal benefit), hydralazine (arteriolar dilator but reduces renal perfusion/causes reflex tachycardia), nitroglycerin (venodilator, minimal arterial/renal effect), and phenylephrine (alpha-1 agonist - vasoCONSTRICTOR, contraindicated).

eliminations.label: Esmolol - beta blocker, no vasodilation/renal benefit
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a short-acting cardioselective beta-1 antagonist (lowers heart rate/contractility). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is not a vasodilator and does not improve renal perfusion or cause natriuresis. ✅ Correct if: aortic dissection/rate control in hypertensive emergency.

eliminations.label: Hydralazine - reduces renal perfusion, reflex tachycardia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a direct ARTERIOLAR vasodilator. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it does NOT dilate renal arterioles and may DECREASE renal perfusion with sodium/fluid retention and reflex sympathetic activation (tachycardia); it doesn't provide the natriuresis described. ✅ Correct if: adjunct vasodilation (e.g., preeclampsia) without the renal-perfusion benefit.

eliminations.label: Nitroglycerin - venodilator, minimal renal effect
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a rapid-acting venodilator that reduces preload/cardiac output. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes only minimal arterial dilation and doesn't improve renal perfusion; it's used mainly for myocardial ischemia/pulmonary edema. ✅ Correct if: hypertensive emergency with ACS/pulmonary edema.

eliminations.label: Phenylephrine - vasoconstrictor (contraindicated)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an alpha-1 adrenergic agonist that RAISES vascular resistance. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes vasoCONSTRICTION and is used for hypotension/shock - contraindicated in hypertensive emergency. ✅ Correct if: hypotension/shock requiring a pressor.

reasoning: Severe hypertension with end-organ damage (encephalopathy, papilledema, renal injury) = hypertensive emergency
The chosen IV drug dilates arterioles AND improves renal perfusion with natriuresis
This unique profile matches fenoldopam, a selective dopamine-1 receptor agonist
mechanism: A HYPERTENSIVE EMERGENCY is severe hypertension (usually >=180/120 mm Hg) WITH acute END-ORGAN DAMAGE (here encephalopathy with confusion, retinal PAPILLEDEMA, and acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine), requiring prompt but CONTROLLED IV blood pressure reduction. FENOLDOPAM is a short-acting, selective peripheral DOPAMINE-1 (D1) RECEPTOR AGONIST with little effect on alpha- or beta-adrenergic receptors. D1 activation stimulates adenylyl cyclase and raises intracellular cAMP, causing VASODILATION of most arterial beds and a corresponding fall in blood pressure. Importantly, RENAL VASODILATION is especially prominent, so fenoldopam INCREASES RENAL PERFUSION, urine output, and NATRIURESIS (sodium excretion) - making it particularly useful in hypertensive emergency with renal insufficiency. The distractors lack this profile: esmolol (beta-1 blocker, no vasodilation), hydralazine (arteriolar dilator that can reduce renal perfusion and cause reflex tachycardia/fluid retention), nitroglycerin (venodilator, minimal arterial/renal effect), and phenylephrine (alpha-1 vasoconstrictor, contraindicated).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Pharm > hypertensive emergency agents: fenoldopam (D1 agonist -> arteriolar + renal vasodilation, natriuresis; good with renal insufficiency); also nitroprusside, labetalol/esmolol, nicardipine; hydralazine reduces renal perfusion; phenylephrine is a vasoconstrictor.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Arteriolar dilation + improved renal perfusion/natriuresis = fenoldopam (dopamine-1 agonist).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on hypertensive emergency, fenoldopam, dopamine-1 receptor, natriuresis, or arteriolar vasodilation? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Esmolol = beta blocker (no vasodilation); hydralazine reduces renal perfusion; nitroglycerin = venodilator; phenylephrine = vasoconstrictor.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: fenoldopam = D1 agonist for hypertensive emergency; arteriolar + renal vasodilation + natriuresis (useful in renal insufficiency).

keywords.back: Selective D1 receptor agonist -> cAMP -> arteriolar (+ renal) vasodilation
Does not dilate renal arterioles; may decrease renal perfusion
Alpha-1 agonist (vasoconstrictor) - contraindicated in HTN emergency

firstAid.detail: Pharm: D1 agonist; arteriolar + renal vasodilation + natriuresis.
Pharm > esmolol, hydralazine, nitroglycerin, phenylephrine differ.
Pharm > fenoldopam preferred when renal function is a concern.

memoryHook: Fenoldopam works the DOPAMINE-1 switch to open arteries AND flush the kidneys (more perfusion + sodium out) - the go-to IV drug for a hypertensive emergency with bad kidneys.
